{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=active+inference+epistemic+curiosity+exploration+autonomous+agent+problem+selection&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1007/s10458-025-09702-y\", \"title\": [\"Correction: Epistemic selection of costly alternatives: the case of participatory budgeting\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/s10458-025-09702-y\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 4, 29]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/springerreference_301925\", \"title\": [\"Epistemic Curiosity\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/springerreference_301925\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/s10458-024-09683-4\", \"title\": [\"Information gathering in POMDPs using active inference\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/s10458-024-09683-4\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 11, 7]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.31234/osf.io/tqf9s_v1\", \"title\": [\"Contextually Attuned Understanding of Epistemic Curiosity in Early Childhood: An Emic Exploration in Nepal\"], \"abstract\": \"

Child-centered and play-based education interventions, increasingly adopted worldwide, often aim to foster epistemic curiosity – the desire for new information – to enhance children’s learning. Dominant Western frameworks conceptualize curiosity as expressed through independent exploration and proactive questioning, treating these behaviors as prototypical indicators of curiosity. However, this characterization is largely derived from research in high-income Western contexts, raising concerns about its cross-cultural validity in non-Western low- and middle-income countries. This qualitative study examines how epistemic curiosity is expressed and interpreted in early childhood classrooms in Nepal. We analyzed data from focus groups with parents and child development experts, interviews with teachers, and classroom observations. Findings revealed expressions of curiosity that extend beyond Western prototypes, particularly attentive information-seeking, such as focused listening. These attentive behaviors were socially valued because they aligned with relational norms emphasizing respect and harmony. By conceptualizing curiosity as a universal construct with context-adaptive manifestations shaped by cultural and sociodemographic dynamics, this study advances a more inclusive framework for studying curiosity across diverse contexts. It challenges indicators that privilege independence and psychological autonomy as the primary expressions of curiosity. This study also highlights auxiliary skills that operate alongside curiosity and variation in adults’ perceptions across demographic contexts.
